owner_gates.action_requiring_explicit_owner_approval: Changing repo visibility (public to private, or any other change)
Rewriting Git history or deleting branches/tags/releases

Adding collaborators or CI deploy credentials

private_source_and_license.requirement: GitHub source repository must be private; only owner and explicitly authorized collaborators may access it.
No public forks, public contributions, public source archives, public development artifacts, public internal docs, research, plans or internal tooling.
No CONTRIBUTING.md inviting outside contributions, no 'open source' wording anywhere, no public issue tracker for source.

Never change repository visibility automatically: prepare runbook and stop to ask owner for explicit approval. Same for history rewrites, force-pushes, repo deletion, collaborator changes and secret rotation.
Original code is proprietary, all rights reserved. No MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL or any open-source license on Keel's own code.
Users receive permission to install and use the binary under an EULA; no source rights and no redistribution rights.
Third-party obligations (dependencies, fonts, icons, models, voices, assets, reference-repo snippets) keep their own licenses, notices and attribution.

architecture_constraints.requirement: No Supabase, Firebase, Postgres, Redis, Tauri, Node/Bun backend, PGlite or hosted vector DB; no hosted backend of any kind required to run Keel.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §5.1 Locked decisions

architecture_constraints.requirement: Existing data preserved via migrations; private repo and proprietary license.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §5.1 Locked decisions

architecture_constraints.requirement: API layer is /api/v2 compatible plus /api/keel/v1; renderer talks to Python daemon over HTTP+SSE on 127.0.0.1 with per-launch bearer token and Origin/Host checks.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules

architecture_constraints.requirement: Separate processes only for Playwright, LSP servers, whisper.cpp, Ollama/llama.cpp, plugin workers and optional container desktop.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules

architecture_constraints.requirement: Core is front-end agnostic: Electron, CLI, SDK, IDE bridges and an MCP-server surface drive the same loop.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 1

architecture_constraints.requirement: Providers are leaves: one provider-neutral message/tool/usage model; tool calling, streaming, thinking and effort are optional capabilities; a model with none still works as a text agent.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 2

architecture_constraints.requirement: Never re-send a partially delivered response; preserve output, warn, do not retry.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 3

architecture_constraints.requirement: Tool results have two renderings (model string, typed UI/audit payload); errors and denials are data, not exceptions.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 4

architecture_constraints.requirement: Output-size ladder: large outputs go to a session file with inline preview, on success and failure.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 5

architecture_constraints.requirement: Two permission tiers. Tier 1: deny/ask/allow, first match wins, wildcards. Tier 2 (non-configurable): protected-path table (test fails if changed), destructive-command analyzer on resolved command, consent-required tools, dangerous-mode interlock. No rule, hook, plugin, policy file or setting reaches Tier 2.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 6

architecture_constraints.requirement: Compaction is a structured record with thrash detector and three-rung overflow ladder.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 7

architecture_constraints.requirement: Model roles: main, summarizer, title, classifier.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 8

architecture_constraints.requirement: Dollar caps degrade to token caps for local models, never to unlimited.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 9

architecture_constraints.requirement: Subagents are a trust boundary: exact tool allowlist, worktree isolation, depth/concurrency caps, reports scanned for instruction-shaped text.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 10

architecture_constraints.requirement: MCP failures reach three audiences: operator status, typed errors, model note.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 11

architecture_constraints.requirement: Instruction files merge, never suppress (AGENTS.md plus Keel's own), with a diagnostic naming sources; subdirectory rules lazy-load.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 12

architecture_constraints.requirement: Read-before-edit via observed-paths set restored on resume; edits are exact-match, UTF-8 safe.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 13

architecture_constraints.requirement: Daemon authenticates even on localhost and rejects foreign Origin/Host.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 14

architecture_constraints.requirement: Dormant-until-configured integrations: unset key parks quietly, revives on hot-reload (/reload or settings save), nothing crash-loops.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 15

architecture_constraints.requirement: Entitlement seam: every feature that could be gated asks entitlements.has('feature.id'); only provider today is AllowAllEntitlements; no license keys, network checks or feature locks (G6).
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 16

architecture_constraints.requirement: Managed-policy seam: optional signed or OS-protected keel-policy.json may tighten settings (disable providers, force offline, pin update server, restrict connectors) but can never loosen Tier 2.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 17

architecture_constraints.requirement: No mandatory accounts, no mandatory telemetry. Crash reports and traces stay local; the only unprompted network call is the disable-able update check.
architecture_constraints.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §6 Target architecture / Design rules design rule 18

architecture_constraints.requirement: JSONC + schema config, provider/model naming, bundled offline provider catalog; existing SQLite file kept with forward-only numbered migrations and automatic backup/integrity check before each migration.

distribution_rules.requirement: The website is the public face: product info, capabilities, screenshots, downloads, install instructions, user docs, latest version, update/release notes.
Website must not expose: source repo link, private dev docs, internal research, credentials, internal build artifacts, implementation details.
Users download and install without ever touching GitHub or the source repository.
Platforms: Windows installer; macOS Apple Silicon; macOS Intel; Linux AppImage, DEB, RPM.
Every release has: version, SHA-256 checksums, release manifest, integrity verification, update checks, secure update download, rollback, install and upgrade instructions.
Private repo may do development, CI/CD and release automation; pipelines publish only approved, allowlisted artifacts. No private repo credentials, source archives or CI secrets ever leave it.
Target state is a private repo; flipping it private before a new feed exists breaks old clients and the download page, so order of operations matters.
distribution_rules.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §4.2 Findings needing action now; Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §0 Non-negotiable owner requirements §0.1

distribution_rules.requirement: D5 primary distribution host: Keel website domain rewriting to a public binaries-only repository (default name 'keel-releases': installers, manifest, checksums, signatures, release notes only). Alternatives: GitHub Pages from that repo, Codeberg, SourceForge, self-hosted static server. Re-verify free-tier terms, size limits and commercial-use terms; Vercel free Hobby tier is non-commercial, so migrate the site before charging anyone.

D3 signing (free reality): Windows - SignPath Foundation unavailable for proprietary software, ship unsigned with documented SmartScreen steps, SHA-256 + Ed25519 verification, winget/Scoop manifests; macOS - Developer ID/notarization needs paid Apple membership, ship unsigned/ad-hoc with documented first-run (right-click Open / xattr), Homebrew custom tap; Linux - Ed25519/GPG-signed artifacts and signed APT/RPM repo (self-hosted static files).
D1 EULA identity, D2 provenance cleanup, D4 Duet definition, D6 trademark check, D7 extension/SDK docs private by default remain open owner decisions.

CI: GitHub Actions on the private repo; free private-repo minutes are limited and macOS/Windows runners use multiplied minutes (verify current numbers). Mitigate with heavy matrix on release tags only, caching, optional free self-hosted runners on owner machines.

Distribution package choices: Electron + electron-builder (NSIS/MSI, dmg, AppImage, deb, rpm), Python via PyInstaller or Nuitka; verification of each license; update feed hosted on public binaries-only repo behind website rewrite; website static for now, migrate if free tier forbids commercial use.

Gates apply to distribution: G1 repo visibility, G2 history/tag/release deletion, G3 first public binary release from new endpoint, G4 collaborators/CI deploy credentials, G7 public extension/SDK docs.
Excluded: hosted share links/infra (replaced by local read-only HTML/Markdown session export); no feature that sends user code to a Keel-operated server.
distribution_rules.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §7 Capability harvest; Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §7.6 Not taken

distribution_rules.requirement: Referenced but absent from the supplied master-plan file: §12-16, §13 v4-to-v5 mapping, Appendices A-D (EULA draft, repo-visibility runbook, packaging and release). Distribution rules above are only those present in §§0-11.

free_first_rules.requirement: Keel stays free to use, local-first and offline-capable: it boots and completes a coding task with no network, no account, no API key, using a local model (CI-enforced).
Architecture must be ready for later free distribution by choice, optional paid plans, premium features, commercial licensing, enterprise and private organizational deployment (M24).
Do not implement payments, subscriptions, license-key enforcement, feature locks or mandatory accounts unless the owner explicitly asks (gate G6).
No paid third-party service anywhere in the plan. Optional adapters for services the user already has are allowed, never required, never bundled, never defaulted on.

Free path defaults: Ollama/llama.cpp/OpenAI-compatible local servers; SQLite WAL + FTS5 + optional sqlite-vec; keyring master key + AES-256-GCM; Playwright + Chromium; optional Podman/Docker Engine (never required); pyright/tsserver/gopls/rust-analyzer/tree-sitter; whisper.cpp/Piper/Kokoro/silero-vad; own idempotent scheduler tick; local OpenTelemetry-shaped spans.
'Offline' means works without internet after install; verify licenses and terms at selection time.
free_first_rules.source: Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §8 Free-only implementation choices; Keel_Master_Plan_v5.md §3.2 Evidence rules

Excluded on purpose: agent-controlled payments, unofficial WhatsApp libraries, any feature sending user code to a Keel-operated server.
macOS notarization and SignPath OSS signing are not available for free/proprietary distribution; ship unsigned with documented verification steps and revisit only if owner accepts paid options.
